title: Qwen Go Fully Opens AI Call-on-Behalf Service, Supporting Reservations, Inquiries, and Scheduled Outbound Calls

content_html:
Alibaba's Qwen Go has fully opened its AI proxy calling service. Users no longer need to dial numbers themselves and can complete phone communication through the AI assistant. Users only need to tell Qwen whom to call and what they need; after authorization is granted, Qwen can contact restaurants to book private rooms, ask hotels about lost items, contact couriers to confirm delivery progress, and more, then report the results after the call ends. In addition, the feature supports scheduled proxy calls, allowing outbound calling tasks to be carried out at times set by the user.

In terms of security mechanisms, Qwen proxy calls require user authorization. During calls, it proactively states that it is an AI assistant, and an outbound-call security protection mechanism screens and blocks risky requests.

This feature rollout further expands Qwen's capabilities from information Q&A to real-world task execution, enabling the AI assistant to connect with offline merchants and service staff through phone channels and complete practical matters such as bookings, inquiries, and communication. It also reflects the trend of AI agents extending into daily life service scenarios.
